title: Decide the publication status of every downloadable file
statement: Each file served for download is recorded as intended for the index, intended to be reachable but excluded from the index, or not intended to be public at all, and the response it returns matches that record.
rationale: Files accumulate in asset directories without anyone deciding whether they should be public, so the default becomes whatever the server does, which is usually to serve them.
implementation: Enumerate what the origin actually serves rather than what the repository intends, and reconcile that list against the recorded status. Move files that should not be public behind authorization rather than only marking them excluded.

verification.method: Request every discovered document address without credentials and compare the returned status and exclusion header against its recorded publication status.

caution: An exclusion directive keeps a file out of a cooperating index; it does not keep the file private. Anything genuinely confidential needs authorization, and this record reports that distinction rather than blurring it.

sources.title: Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications

title: Give each published document an accurate internal title
statement: A document's embedded title describes its contents and matches the heading a reader sees on opening it, rather than retaining a template name, a path, or the name of the file it was copied from.
rationale: The embedded title is what appears in a result listing and in a reader's window, so a document titled after its template is presented to everyone under a name that describes nothing.
implementation: Set the title in the generator that produces the document rather than correcting it afterwards, and take the value from the same field that renders the visible heading.

verification.method: Extract embedded titles from served documents and report those that are empty, hold a template or path string, or disagree with the document's first heading.

caution: Search platforms document that a document's own title may be used in a listing without specifying how, so the requirement that it be accurate is this registry's inference from that use and the record is tier B.

sources.title: Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications

title: Nominate one address when a document duplicates a page
statement: Where the same material exists as both a web page and a downloadable file, one of the two is nominated as the version to index and the other declares that nomination through a link header.
rationale: Leaving both versions unnominated lets the platform choose, and it frequently chooses the file, so readers arriving from search get a download instead of the page the site maintains.
implementation: Prefer the page as the nominated version where one exists, since it can carry navigation and be corrected in place, and emit the header from the route that serves the file.

verification.method: Identify page and document pairs covering the same material and confirm the served link header on the file names the nominated address.

title: Serve each document with its correct media type
statement: A document response declares the registered media type for its format, and declares a disposition only where a download rather than in-place viewing is intended.
rationale: A file served as a generic byte stream is treated as an opaque download rather than a readable document, so its text is never extracted and the reader gets a save dialog instead of the content.
implementation: Map extensions to registered types once in the serving layer rather than per route, and set a disposition deliberately for the cases that should download rather than as a blanket default.

verification.method: Request each document address and compare the declared media type and disposition against the file's actual format as detected from its contents.

sources.title: RFC 6266: Use of the Content-Disposition Header Field

title: Strip authoring metadata before a document is published
statement: A document leaving for a public address carries no revision history, no tracked changes, no author or organisation fields left by the authoring tool, and no content hidden behind a layer or a cropped region.
rationale: Authoring tools retain removed text and internal identities inside the file, so a document that looks finished when opened still carries the material someone deleted from it.
implementation: Run a flattening or sanitising step in the publication pipeline so no document reaches a public address without passing through it, rather than relying on authors to clean files by hand.

verification.method: Inspect published documents for retained revision data, authoring identity fields, and text present in the file but not visible when rendered.

caution: That a published file discloses everything it contains rather than only what it displays is a property of file formats, not of any search platform, so no citation applies. Detection covers the retained-data shapes the inspection recognises rather than proving a file is clean.

title: Publish documents whose text can be extracted
statement: A public document exposes its text as text, with a reading order and headings that follow the visual structure, rather than as page images requiring recognition to read.
rationale: A scanned document is an image to every reader that is not a pair of eyes, so its contents reach neither assistive technology, nor search, nor anyone using find-in-page.
implementation: Generate documents from their source rather than by scanning a printout, and where only a scan exists, add a recognised text layer and check the resulting reading order rather than trusting it.

verification.method: Extract text from each served document and report those yielding no text, or yielding a sequence that does not follow the document's visual reading order.

caution: Recognised text can be wrong in ways that look right, so a recognition step is checked against the original rather than assumed correct.
